The 4 apps that I actually use for photography ☕︎
 
Lightroom is where 99% of my editing happens, from exposure to my full cinematic grade.
 
TouchRetouch is for fast cleanups on the go, way quicker than opening Lightroom for a tiny fix.
 
Alpenglow tells me exactly where and when the sun will rise or set, so I’m in the right spot at the right time.
 
SCRL is how I make those satisfying horizontal swipes for my carousels.
 
None of these are groundbreaking on their own, but together they cover planning, shooting, editing and posting. Save this if you’re building your own kit.
 
Got an app you swear by that’s not on here? Drop it below ✍︎

I find it fascinating how quickly we get used to things. Something we once prayed for can strangely start to feel like an ordinary day. I used to dream about finally having a home base. And now that I have one, I’ve got dishes and laundry to do. I guess it’s a good thing we can get used to change, because it means we can adapt and survive difficult seasons. I just wish we were a little slower to get used to the good stuff -  it takes a little more effort to notice.

Eleuthería - What does it mean to be free when you don’t know what you’re trying to escape? 

Perhaps we keep moving because we’re afraid of what we might find in the stillness. We leave places, chase new beginnings, and hope along the way somewhere, something inside us will finally settle. But no matter how far we go, we carry ourselves with us. Maybe freedom isn’t about finding somewhere else to be, but learning that we don’t always have to run from where we are.
